reason: The uploads contain real rainfall but no flood-alert records, and the rainfall span is far shorter than the feature warm-up.

issues.detail: readings not aligned to the 5-minute grid; RainGrid floors them and averages collisions
55 stations over 0.4 days; 99.8% of the slots a complete record would hold

FloodAlertsacrossSingapore.json.value: Confirms the endpoint /v2/real-time/api/weather/flood-alerts and the CAP-derived schema.

RelativeHumidityacrossSingapore.json.note: Documents /v2/real-time/api/relative-humidity. Humidity is not a FloodSense input.

FloodProneAreas.csv.note: National annual aggregate. Not a geospatial layer and not a label source.

blockers.detail: 0 flood-alert records were supplied, so the target variable does not exist. Accuracy of a classifier with no labels is undefined.
Rainfall spans 8.4 hours (102 five-minute steps). The feature warm-up alone is 2592 steps (~9 days) for EWM burn-in and 72-hour accumulations.
blockers.pipeline_error: ValueError: warm-up (2592 steps) exceeds the record (102 steps)

blockers.detail: A train/validation/test split by time needs enough flood events in every split; 8.4 hours cannot be split three ways.

what_would_unblock: Flood-alert records (not the API spec) covering the same period as the rainfall - the binding constraint.
Rainfall covering at least several months so the warm-up and three-way split fit; the full annual NEA CSVs are ~6.4M rows each.
Network access to api-open.data.gov.sg and data.gov.sg to fetch both automatically.
accuracy_note: Not computed. No labels and insufficient history. No number is reported rather than a fabricated one.
